title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 4
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 4: the oppressed without a comforter, a handful with quietness, two being better than one, and the threefold cord.

questions.text: What did the oppressed lack, according to the first verse?
questions.explanation: The speaker saw the tears of those who were oppressed, and they had no comforter, while power was on the side of their oppressors.

questions.text: Whom did the speaker praise more than the living who are yet alive?
questions.explanation: He says he praised the dead who have been long dead more than the living who are yet alive.

answers.text: The dead who have been long dead

questions.text: What does the fool do when he folds his hands together?
questions.explanation: The verse says the fool folds his hands together and ruins himself.

questions.text: What does this chapter say is better than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind?
questions.explanation: The verse says better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.

questions.text: Why are two better than one, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.

answers.text: Because they have a good reward for their labor
Because they can divide the spoil
Because one can watch while the other sleeps

questions.text: What happens if two fall, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says that if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow, but woe to him who is alone when he falls and has no one to lift him up.

answers.text: A third must come to help
The one will lift up his fellow

questions.text: What do two have if they lie together?
questions.explanation: The verse says that if two lie together, they have warmth, but how can one keep warm alone?

questions.text: What does this chapter say about a threefold cord?
questions.explanation: The verse says a threefold cord is not quickly broken.

answers.text: It is woven by wise hands

questions.text: Who is better than an old and foolish king who no longer knows how to receive admonition?
questions.explanation: The verse says better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who doesn't know how to receive admonition any more.

questions.text: From where did the youth in this chapter come out to be king?
questions.explanation: The verse says that out of prison he came out to be king, and even in his kingdom he was born poor.

answers.text: Out of the house of his father
